text.text: Cisco cBR-8

graphic.text: Cisco cBR-8

text.text: Cisco's cBR-8 is a revolutionary Converged Cable Access Platform (CCAP) that is designed from the ground up to deliver unprecedented performance and scalabilty to 1+ Tbps with current and future access technologies including DOCSIS 3.1 and Remote PHY. cBR-8 is designed as a “hub in a box” platform which integrates many disparate headend functions needed to support the full suite of DOCSIS and MPEG Video services, and integrates with Software Defined Networking (SDN) architectures for greater operational efficiency and faster service velocity.

text.text: Front View

graphic.text: Front View

text.text: The cBR-8 is a 13RU 10-slot chassis featuring a unique design with horizontal card slots to maximize chassis density while maintaining front-to-back airflow. Eight Subscriber Side slots are designed to support current and future access technologies including HFC, Remote PHY, and PON with N+1 redundancy. Two Supervisor card slots enable 1+1 redundancy. The cBR-8 supports hot-swappable AC/DC power supplies and fan modules to maximize system availability.

text.text: RF Line Card

graphic.text: RF Line Card

text.text: The RF Line Card supports up to 8 DS ports and 16 US ports (8x16), with 768 unique DS channels and 64 US channels per card (initially), and flexibility in configuring the number of channels per port. The modular design accommodates two DS modules and one US module per card, which can be independently upgraded to support new technologies including DOCSIS 3.1, or removed for Remote PHY applications.

text.text: Supervisor Card

graphic.text: Supervisor Card

text.text: The Supervisor Card supports up to 200 Gbps data forwarding, high-performance routing and control plane processing, and integrated service intelligence to support a comprehensive suite of high-speed data, voice over IP, and video services. Each Supervisor Card supports redundant 8x10GE ports for WAN connectivity, enabling up to 160 Gbps throughput.

Mid-Plane

text.text: The cBR-8 mid-plane connects the RF Line Cards and Supervisor Cards to the Physical Interface Cards (PICs), and provides flexibility to support a variety of physical interfaces, such as coax, analog optics, 10 GE, and PON. The mid-plane is designed to support 1+ Tbps throughput to ensure longevity even as access network traffic continues to grow at unprecedented rates, and enables integrated RF switching to maximize system availability.

text.text: Power Supply

graphic.text: Power Supply

text.text: The cBR-8 chassis houses six power supply modules which support a total of approximately 9KW (Facilities Requirement). AC and DC modules are supported, with 3+1 or 3+3 redundancy for AC modules, and 4+1 redundancy for DC modules. Each module supports integrated fans at the front and the appropriate receptacle/terminals at the rear, and are hot-swappable to maximize system availability.

text.text: Rear View

graphic.text: Rear View

text.text: All physical interfaces and power supply connections are located at the rear of the cBR-8 chassis. Up to 8 RF Line Card PICs and 2 Supervisor Card PICs are supported. Each RF Line Card PIC and Supervisor Card PIC is connected via the mid-plane to a RF Line Card and Supervisor Card, respectively. The fan modules and power supplies exhaust air at the rear of the chassis.

text.text: RF Line Card PIC supports 8 DS and 16 US coaxial MCX connectors. With N+1 redundancy enabled, the RF Line Card Protect PIC supports integrated RF switching to direct traffic to/from the redundant RF Line Card to the appropriate RF Line Card PIC in the case of a RF Line Card failure.

text.text: Supervisor PIC supports redundant 8x10GE SFP+ ports. With 1+1 redundancy enabled, all 10GE ports remain active on both Supervisor Cards, and traffic is directed to/from the active Supervisor Card.

text.text: Mid-plane design of the cBR-8 provides greater operational efficiency and improved system availability by enabling service providers to upgrade/replace RF Line/Supervisor Cards without touching the physical interfaces. It connects each PIC to the corresponding RF Line/Supervisor Card and also enables a variety of physical interface types to be supported in the future that work with the RF Line/Supervisor Card.
